proposal.title: Restructure external product impacts — Apple Disk II
proposal.reason: Consolidate descriptive content and move assessed product/standard effects into typed impact sections. Preserve historical interfaces, fictional-world boundaries and qualification limits. Evidence: data_storytelling/review_evidence/external-impact-revision/assessment.json.

before.name: Apple Disk II
before.description: Apple Disk II is a storage peripheral for Apple II.

specification.description: Controller-driven 5¼-inch floppy system; the original 13-sector format stores about 114 KB per disk side. The intended host environment is {host}. Interfaces, cabling and software must match that configuration.

Assessment at 1979-12-31. These are conditional commercial comparisons, not measured changes in sales.

{primary_offering}: Disk II is the established same-host disk alternative; retaining Apple disk software can reduce migration work, while FlexiDisk II needs its recorded Apple interface and format qualification.

{related_offering}: The Logix card includes a Disk II-compatible controller path as well as FlexiBUS, so the installed Disk II ecosystem can complement the card as well as compete with a new external drive.

impacted_standards.assumption_description: Compare an Apple II with working Disk II software against the 1979 Logix card and qualified FlexiDisk II configuration.
impacted_standards.comparison_description: Disk II uses an Apple controller/disk interface rather than FlexiBUS; disk-format compatibility alone does not convert the transport.
impacted_standards.outcomes_description: Existing disks and applications create a switching hurdle. Retaining a qualified Disk II path can make incremental FlexiBUS adoption more attractive; no sales uplift is measured.

specification.description: Controller-driven 5¼-inch floppy system; the original 13-sector format stores about 114 KB per disk side. The intended host environment is {host}. Interfaces, cabling and software must match that configuration.

impacted_standards.assumption_description: Assess {historical_product} in its recorded {host} configuration. Compare an Apple II with working Disk II software against the 1979 Logix card and qualified FlexiDisk II configuration.
impacted_standards.comparison_description: Disk II uses an Apple controller/disk interface rather than FlexiBUS; disk-format compatibility alone does not convert the transport. The relationship concerns alternative complete configurations, not proven direct compatibility with this standard.
impacted_standards.outcomes_description: Existing disks and applications create a switching hurdle. Retaining a qualified Disk II path can make incremental FlexiBUS adoption more attractive; no sales uplift is measured.

impacted_products.assumption_description: Assess the recorded {host} configuration with its required controller, cabling and software. Controller-driven 5¼-inch floppy system; the original 13-sector format stores about 114 KB per disk side.
impacted_products.comparison_description: The alternative is a FlexiBUS 5.25-inch drive with recorded Aurelia and Apple II-compatible formats. Apple operation needs the Logix Apple II adapter; matching media formats does not make the electrical interfaces interchangeable. The canonical implementation is {implementation}.
impacted_products.outcomes_description: Disk II is the established same-host disk alternative; retaining Apple disk software can reduce migration work, while FlexiDisk II needs its recorded Apple interface and format qualification. This is a conditional purchase-path assessment, not evidence of measured market share or superior performance.

impacted_products.assumption_description: Assess the recorded {host} configuration with its required controller, cabling and software. Controller-driven 5¼-inch floppy system; the original 13-sector format stores about 114 KB per disk side.
impacted_products.comparison_description: The Logix Apple II adapter includes a Disk II-compatible controller path as well as FlexiBUS. Retaining the native disk path could support an incremental upgrade, subject to drive, firmware and format qualification; the Disk II drive is not thereby a FlexiBUS device. The canonical implementation is {implementation}.

This is a conditional purchase-path assessment, not evidence of measured market share or superior performance.
